title: Ledger entry
description: One line of ledger.jsonl in the private store (design parts 5.4 and 13.1). Append-only: corrections are new events that reference the old one. The ledger is internal as a whole, so lines carry no classification. Events: the ten of part 5.4, plus sent (a question was shown to its decider), logged (a call the orchestrator made without asking) and, for orchestrator continuity, run-started, lease-taken and lease-released (part 13.1). merge-approved records the owner's answer to a batch presented in owner merge mode (all of it, or a list), bound to that presentation and written by the session the owner said it in; the session holding the lease applies it. For the watchdog (part 5.2): stalled (a dispatch showed no progress for too long, or passed its deadline, with the ladder step taken), poked (its agent was asked to report its status), interrupted (it was stopped, and continues as a follow-up with its commits kept; it ends the dispatch). For quota pauses (part 12.5): paused (the quota gate stopped autonomous dispatch, with the limit and when its window resets) and resumed. friction (HITLD-595, part 18.4): one sighting of a friction class, read from the harness's record of a session by hitld friction scan, or recorded by the chief of staff as it recognizes one (self_recognized); its ID is its class and its evidence's ID, so a second scan appends nothing. The trust record of the approval is written once, when it is applied. dispatched is recorded before the harness is called; started is recorded when the harness has accepted the dispatch, and carries its harness_ref. Version 2 (HITLD-82) renamed claimed to started, question to asked, released to unclaimed, outcome to result and handle to harness_ref; the reader takes a version 1 line in the old names, permanently, since the ledger is never rewritten.

id.description: Unique per event, so applying an event is idempotent.

run.description: The run this event belongs to; on run-started, the new run's ID.

role.description: executor, acceptance, adversary, reviewer, triager, and so on.

hitld_version.description: The HITLd version (plugin before schema version 2).

result.description: How the attempt ended. For reported: done, partial or blocked. For verified: pass or fail.

defects.description: For a failed verification: the defect count.

tokens.description: On reported: what the dispatch cost, output tokens plus fresh input (uncached input and cache writes), never cache reads; null when nothing gave a figure. tokens_source says where it came from. What the executor said its own run cost is never this figure: it is self_reported_tokens.

tokens_source.description: On reported, beside tokens (HITLD-438): where the figure came from. session-record: measured, from the harness's own record of the executor's session (an interactive dispatch). result-file: measured, from a headless run's result. notification: the usage block of the harness's completion notification (undocumented). typed: typed by hand, because the harness record was not available; a correction (hitld ledger correct-tokens) is typed. The estimator weighs a measured figure over a typed one. Absent on a line written before it, whose source is not known.

usage.description: On reported, when the harness's record or result gave them (HITLD-438): its counts kept apart, cache reads included, and the cost it reports. tokens is input_tokens plus cache_write_tokens plus output_tokens.

cache_read_tokens.description: Input read from the cache: kept apart, never counted in tokens.

cost_usd.description: The cost the harness reports, in US dollars.

self_reported_tokens.description: On reported (HITLD-438): the token figure the executor's report gives for its own run. A guess, since an executor has no meter for its own usage: kept for comparison with the measured figure, and never read as the cost by the summary, the digest or the estimator.

estimate_tokens.description: On dispatched: the token estimate the dispatch started with, set at sizing; on reported, a copy of it. A follow-up's dispatched carries none: the item's earlier one stands. It is read capped at dispatch.estimate_max_multiple times the tier's default, unless the item set it (HITLD-450). A correction (hitld ledger correct-estimate) is a dispatched event that corrects the original, and is read in its place.

estimate_source.description: On dispatched, beside estimate_tokens (HITLD-450): where the estimate came from. item: the item's own estimate_tokens. history: the median of similar past completions. default: the tier's default (dispatch.default_estimates). typed: typed by hand, as a correction (hitld ledger correct-estimate) is. Absent on a line written before it, whose source is not known.

estimate_samples.description: On dispatched, beside estimate_source (HITLD-450): how many similar past completions with a token count there were when it was sized, so an estimate that rested on one record shows in the ledger itself. 0 for an item's own estimate and a typed one. Absent on a line written before it.

corrects.description: The ID of an earlier event this one corrects.

session.description: The orchestrator session: on run-started and lease-taken, the session that now holds the lease; on lease-released, the session that gave it up or was retired. On friction: the session whose record it was read from. On logged, and on any other event a session writes without a dispatch (asked, sent, answered, verified, merged, reverted): the session that wrote it.

host.description: The machine the executor runs on (dispatched, claimed), or the orchestrator's machine (run-started, lease-taken, lease-released). On logged, and on any other event a session writes without a dispatch: the machine that session runs on.

harness.description: The harness adapter ID, on started.

harness_ref.description: The harness's own reference for the dispatch (an agent ID, a process ID, a task URL), on started. On run-started and lease-taken: the orchestrator session's own reference, where the harness gives one, so wakes can be sent to it.

serial_resources.description: Serial resources the dispatch holds (design part 13.2), on dispatched.

touches.description: On dispatched: the touches the overlap rule and the brief used, the item's own or, when it has none, derived from its text and the repository (HITLD-136).

touches_source.description: On dispatched: item when the touches are the item's own, derived when they were derived from its text. Writing touches on the item corrects derived ones.

decision.description: The decision item a question, its showing or its answer is about.

delivery.description: On sent: interrupt when the question was sent at once, outside a digest, which uses one of the person's interrupts_per_day; digest when it went in a digest. A sent line without it counts as a digest.

via.description: On answered: default when no one answered and the decision took its default (its default_if_unanswered passed its deadline, or the person's digest was full and it is easy to undo). The answer is not the person's, so it is left out of decision latency.

text.description: On logged: the call, in a sentence, as the orchestrator decided it without asking. The digest lists it, and the owner can reverse it by this event's ID. On answered: the answer as written in the decision item, which a merge under the owner's delegation checks a changed answer against.

area.description: On logged: the area the call belongs to, when it has one. On dispatched and stalled: the item's first area, so stall rates can be read per area.

mode.description: On dispatched, for tier 3: headless (a background run whose completion reaches the dispatching session) or interactive (its own session, which the chief of staff starts).

reason.description: On lease-released: handover (the holder wrote the hand-over and gave the lease up) or ended (the chief of staff saw the session end without one, and retired it). On stalled: no_progress (nothing observed for the dispatch's stall time), deadline (past its start-to-finish deadline), limit (cut off by a usage limit: quiet across a quota pause, found after the reset) or exited (a headless run's process ended without a result). On resumed: reset (the limiting window reset) or budget (the gate allows dispatch again before the reset: a raised budget or reserve, or new readings). On reported: executor-permissions (the report showed commands the contract requires, hitld, node, npm or git, refused by the executor's permission mode; the result is blocked, and its notes name the commands).

step.description: On stalled: the step of the watchdog's ladder taken: poke (ask the same agent for its status), follow-up (interrupt it and continue it as a follow-up, keeping its commits), abandon (end it and dispatch the item afresh) or ask (a question for the owner, after repeated failures).

limit.description: On paused: the quota limit that stopped dispatch, by its id.

resets_at.description: On paused: when the limiting window resets, from the latest reading (the status line's resets_at) or the declared reset. Absent when neither gives it.

branches.description: On merge-approved: the presented branches the owner approved.

presented_at.description: On merge-approved: when the batch it answers was presented; with commit (the batch's tested commit), it names that presentation.

by.description: On lease-released and merge-approved: the session that recorded it (the holder itself, or the chief of staff).

policy_hash.description: On run-started: the hash of the effective policy.json the run started with.

scope.description: On run-started: what the run covers.

friction_class.description: On friction: the class (core/lib/friction/friction.mjs). Deterministic classes are read from the session record with no model; semantic ones (owner-correction, repeated-instruction, owner-did-work, bundled-question, already-decided) by an independent reader, or by the chief of staff as it recognizes one.

source.description: On friction: whose action shows it: the owner, a delegate or the system.

evidence.description: On friction: where it shows, by reference: the session record's ID for the event or message and its time, and for a semantic class a short exact quote. Never more of the text.

decisions.description: On friction: the owner decisions settled by then (answered events, not a default), so rates are taken per decision, not per day.

cause.description: On friction, when the class has one: what caused it, such as restart for a question a restart dropped, or box-open for a reply written while a question box was open.

confidence.description: On friction of a semantic class read by the independent reader: its confidence, from 0 to 1.

self_recognized.description: On friction: true when the chief of staff recorded it as it recognized it, so the independent reader's reading can be compared with it.
